newsitem.title: KYRGYZSTAN: Kazakh, Kyrgyz, Uzbek leaders to meet in Bishkek.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh, Kyrgyz, Uzbek leaders to meet in Bishkek.

text.p: The leaders of the Central Asian republics of Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan will meet in the Kyrgyz capital Bishkek on Thursday for a two-day summit aimed at improving ties between the three former Soviet states.
The Kyrgyz Foreign Ministry's press service said on Wednesday the three leaders were likely to sign a treaty of "eternal friendship" on Friday.
They are also expected to discuss the work of the jointly run Central Asian Bank set up in 1994.
The three states have also sent peacekeeping troops, along with Russia, to neighbouring Tajikistan, which has been torn apart by a four-year civil war.
In 1993, the three former Soviet republics formed the Central Asian Union, designed to strengthen regional economic integration. Regional neighbours Turkmenistan and Tajikistan are not members.
